post.title: Deep Learning Architectures: CNNs, RNNs, and Transformers
post.subtitle: Choosing the right deep learning architecture matters more than model size. Learn when to use CNNs, RNNs, and Transformers.
post.brief: CNNs, RNNs, and Transformers solve different kinds of pattern problems. CNNs are great for spatial data like images, RNNs handle ordered sequences, and Transformers shine when long-range context matters. Choosing the right architecture often matters more than adding more layers.

This walkthrough focuses on **The Right Tool for the Job: Why Architecture Choice Matters**.

Before making a design choice, clarify:

- At ImageNet 2012 , AlexNet won the image recognition challenge with 85% accuracy — beating every hand-engineered computer vision system by more than 10 percentage points.
- The team hadn't built better features by hand; they'd trained deep convolutional layers to learn the features automatically from raw pixels.
- That single result launched the deep learning era and proved that architecture design matters more than manual feature engineering.

**Concepts in play:** deep-learning-foundations, caching, api-gateway, api-security-oauth2

## Stage 1 — Data Shape Drives Architecture Selection

- The single most important rule: match architecture to data structure .
- Pick the architecture family that matches your data shape.
- Choose model size within that family.
- A larger model in the wrong family still underperforms a smaller model with the right inductive bias.

*Applies **deep-learning-foundations** to the decision above.*

## Stage 2 — CNN, RNN, and Transformer Internals Side by Side

- Every architecture follows the same high-level loop: Input tensor → architecture-specific blocks → prediction head → loss → backpropagation → weight update.
- CNN block: small filters slide across a spatial grid.
- Early layers detect edges; later layers detect shapes and objects.
- Weight sharing across positions gives CNNs parameter efficiency on image data.

*Applies **caching** to the decision above.*

**Observable outcome:** Weight sharing across positions gives CNNs parameter efficiency on image data.

## Stage 3 — Deep Dive: How Attention Replaces Recurrence

- The key Transformer innovation is scaled dot-product attention : each token computes query, key, and value vectors.
- Attention scores are dot products of queries against all keys, scaled by √d to prevent vanishing gradients, then softmaxed into weights that blend value vectors.
- This lets the model attend to any position in one step—no sequential bottleneck.
- 📊 Transformer Encoder: From Tokens to Contextual Output Each encoder layer refines token representations by mixing context from all other tokens via attention, then applying a position-wise feed-forward transformation.

*Applies **api-gateway** to the decision above.*

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Input Tokens] --> B[Token Embedding]
    B --> C[Positional Encoding]
    C --> D[Multi-Head Attention]
    D --> E[Add & Norm]
    E --> F[Feed Forward]
    F --> G[Add & Norm]
    G --> H[Repeat N Layers]
    H --> I[Output Projection]
    I --> J[Softmax]
```

**Observable outcome:** 📊 Transformer Encoder: From Tokens to Contextual Output Each encoder layer refines token representations by mixing context from all other tokens via attention, then applying a position-wise feed-forward transformation.

## Stage 5 — Real-World Applications: Where Each Architecture Lives in Production

- CNNs: defect detection in manufacturing, medical imaging triage, OCR preprocessing, real-time video classification on edge devices.
- RNNs: forecasting and streaming anomaly detection in telemetry pipelines; still competitive on constrained hardware where Transformer overhead is prohibitive.
- Transformers: search ranking, document understanding, code completion, multilingual NLP, any task requiring understanding of long-form text.
- A support-ticket router might use a Transformer encoder for semantic features and a lightweight recurrent branch for short metadata sequences — combining both views for the final routing decision.

*Applies **deep-learning-foundations** to the decision above.*
